title: Budget outcomes
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest point, e-fiscal, covers how spending and tax changes shift aggregate demand, but it does not teach deficits and surpluses or how to judge a policy stance from changes in the budget outcome, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Budget outcomes
card: Government spending is greater than government revenue in the year. The gap is the size of the deficit.
Government revenue is greater than government spending in the year. The extra is the size of the surplus.
Compare the outcome from one year to the next. A move towards deficit (or a smaller surplus) means policy is expansionary, as the government adds more to total spending in the economy.
A move towards surplus (or a smaller deficit) means policy is contractionary, as the government adds less. A deficit alone does not tell you which way policy is moving.
draft.remember: Look at the change in the budget outcome, not just the outcome itself.

a.q: A government's budget moves from a surplus of $2 billion to a deficit of $8 billion. What does this change show?
opts: Policy has not changed, as the budget is in deficit
Revenue has risen faster than spending
a.why: The budget moved towards deficit, so the government is adding more to total spending. That is expansionary policy. Revenue rising faster than spending would move the budget towards surplus, which is the opposite.
a.clue: Which direction did the budget outcome move?

b.q: Last year Country A ran a deficit of $30 billion. This year its deficit is $10 billion. Which statement is best supported by the change?
opts: Policy is expansionary, because there is still a deficit
Policy is neutral, because the budget did not reach surplus
b.why: The deficit shrank, so the budget moved towards surplus and the government is adding less to total spending. That is contractionary. A deficit is still there, but the change is what shows the direction of policy.
b.clue: Compare this year with last year, not with zero.
